Information received since May indicates continued labor‑market strength and moderate growth, while 12‑month inflation is running below the 2% objective. In line with New Keynesian policy rules (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Taylor rule), the FOMC delivered a gradual, still‑accommodative rate increase and emphasized data dependence and its symmetric inflation goal. Persistently low market‑based inflation compensation and little‑changed longer‑term expectations (Svensson and Woodford, expectations management) argue for caution, even as forward guidance and interest‑on‑reserves/floor‑system implementation (Goodfriend; Cúrdia and Woodford) keep the funds rate within the 1–1.25% target range. The planned balance‑sheet normalization is consistent with the view that QE mainly works via term‑premium channels and can be unwound gradually without derailing activity. Overall tone: modestly positive on growth and employment, cautious on inflation.
